requirements.statement: The high-risk plants set's decisions ledger holds an entry for every decision that changes a plants behaviour the ledger already rules on, added as a new numbered entry naming the entry it supersedes, with the earlier entry kept in the ledger marked superseded and the subject it rules on re-stamped with the new resolution, who decided it and the new entry's id.
requirements.why: The ledger is the only place a plants ruling lives, and every conflict entry and every behaviour carries a pointer to it rather than its own answer, so a plants page changed without its entry leaves the set's own record saying the opposite of what the service does.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the ledger's 97 entries carry no decision from this programme at all: they settle no content, wording, layout or component question of the design release, name neither the notification list's reframing nor a party picker's page size, and the seven superseded entries were every one of them replaced by the set's own owner rulings (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-001, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-005, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-183-m1, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-184).

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants journey specification's entry for each page, obligation and behaviour says what that page, obligation or behaviour does in the service, so a reader of the specification and a user of the journey see the same thing.
requirements.why: The specification is the plants set's contract and the tests linked to its scenarios are its evidence, so an entry that still reads the old way makes the contract false and the evidence point at behaviour nobody has.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the specification states the journey as it stood before this programme: the overview page is headed Overview with four numbered groups and five row statuses, the read-only view carries no Copy as new, the page order ends at check your answers from the contact page, and the picker, list and status-strip entries describe today's layout (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-019, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-020, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-050, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-067, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-070, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-078, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-080). It also still marks all seven of its sources as being extracted, says the whole-journey fixture and the contract-test table do not exist when both do, and holds an empty happy-path fixture beside it (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-010, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-227, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-228, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-229).

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants conflicts register's entry for a recorded disagreement names the decision that settled it, with that decision's resolution and who made it.
requirements.why: The register carries a pointer to the ledger and never its own answer, so an entry left pointing at a withdrawn decision reads as settled when it is not.
requirements.deltaNote: Today all 40 entries point at the set's own panel or owner rulings, 33 to the panel and 7 to the owner, and none of them points at a decision of this programme (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-008, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-009).

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants panel's evidence stays as it is when a ruling changes: its eight dockets, its 83 rulings with their rationale, spec changes and dissent, its reconciliation entries, its critic report and its panel README.
requirements.why: They record why each plants decision was taken, so a reopened question starts from the argument rather than the outcome; editing them would rewrite the reasoning instead of adding to it.
requirements.deltaNote: The set's own rule already says that changing a ruling leaves rulings.json and critic.json alone and edits the ledger and its subject in one commit (repo-plantsfrontend-p17-005).

requirements.statement: A document in the high-risk plants set's docs folder that states a behaviour of the journey says what the journey does, and changes in the same increment as the behaviour it describes.
requirements.why: The set's own documentation-drift work records that a document stating something the code does not do is a defect, because a second, false specification is read as though it were current.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the guides describe the journey as it stood before this programme: the served-surface reference's dashboard and picker description, the flow guide's sections, task rows, Back rules and caption map, the features guide's save-actions and view-header description, and the copy-status table (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-001, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-002, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-006, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-075, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-090, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-108, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-116, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-125, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-155, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-189).

requirements.statement: In the high-risk plants frontend the consignment contact page's two return controls read "Save and return to overview" and "Cancel and return to overview".
requirements.why: A return control names the page it opens, which is headed Overview, and every other page in the plants and live animals journeys names it that way.
requirements.deltaNote: Today they read "Save and return to hub" and "Cancel and return to hub", the one plants page where the internal name Hub reaches the screen (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-077, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-079).

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants notification view header offers Amend and Delete and no Copy as new.
requirements.why: Whether the plants header carries a third action decides whether an increment adds to plants a capability the plants set has parked under its own standing ruling.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants records say the list and the read-only view offer View, Amend and Delete and no Copy as new anywhere, and reusing a previous consignment is parked with no increment of its own (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-131, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-073, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-049).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants address picker lists eight addresses a page, pages beyond eight, restates the address already chosen in an inset above the results, ticks the chosen row, and reads "No addresses match your search." when a search finds none.
requirements.why: Every picker in both journeys pages at the one figure the address book list already uses, and the inset keeps the chosen address on screen when its row is not on the page being read.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants records already describe exactly this (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-078, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-006, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-007, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-008).

requirements.statement: A change mirrored into the high-risk plants journey changes its structure, wording patterns, components and behaviour, and never which questions it asks, which values a field offers or which commodities a rule covers.
requirements.why: The plants journey's data comes from its own statute and policy paper, so a look-and-feel change that moved a question or a value would put the service outside the law it implements.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants set's own standing rulings already say so: the fourth ranks the policy paper and its draft statute above the Confluence pages, the Mural board and the prototype, and the fifth keeps the animals shape only where no plants source gives a reason to diverge (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-007, repo-plantsfrontend-p17-004).

requirements.statement: An increment that changes a high-risk plants page reads that page's maturity level from the page's own page identity module, and treats a page at agreed or readyForLive as signed off.
requirements.why: A change to a signed-off page needs a person's agreement, so an increment has to know which plants pages are signed off before it changes one.
requirements.deltaNote: The engine already reads a page's level and shows it in the phase banner, and agreed or readyForLive already counts as signed off, but the set's docs do not say which pages are at which level (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-064, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-067, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-385).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants page's maturity level changes only through its own reviewed pull request.
requirements.why: Promotion is a person's judgement that the page's behaviour is agreed, so it cannot ride along inside a change that alters the behaviour.
requirements.deltaNote: The set's features guide already says a page's maturity level changes only through a reviewed pull request (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-066).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants notification's late flag is set once, at its first submission from draft, and the confirmation page, the read-only view and the list card read the stored value; a resubmission after an amendment moves the submitted date and leaves the flag alone, and a cancelled amendment restores the snapshot carrying it.
requirements.why: Lateness is judged against the timing the trader was held to when they first notified, so recomputing it from a later submission would change a recorded fact about a submitted notification.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants ledger already rules the late flag a stored system value committed immediately before submitting while the notification is a draft, and read back rather than recomputed (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-018, repo-plantsfrontend-p17-025).

requirements.statement: Every label, hint, option text and error message on a high-risk plants page lives in its own feature's copy pair, and a display-shaped key in the obligation model stops the service starting.
requirements.why: One home for the words means a wording change is a copy change, and the boot guard makes the rule enforceable rather than a convention a change can quietly break.
requirements.deltaNote: The set's obligation-model guide and its three boot guards already hold this (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-086, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-053, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-054).

requirements.statement: A string added to or changed on a high-risk plants page lands in both its feature's English and Welsh copy files with the same leaf paths and value kinds, the Welsh a machine draft headed as unreviewed with no Welsh invented, and the copy-convention and copy-parity checks run over every pair.
requirements.why: The service owes a Welsh version it cannot yet publish, so every string is captured in both files as it is written rather than retrofitted when a translator arrives.
requirements.deltaNote: Every plants feature already carries both copy files under the parity and convention checks, with the Welsh headed as not reviewed by a translator (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-084, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-089, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-190).

requirements.statement: A number more than one high-risk plants feature shows, such as a timing window or a length limit, is written once as a named constant and reaches the copy as a function argument.
requirements.why: A reissued policy paper then changes one constant rather than every sentence that quotes it, and no second copy of the number can drift.
requirements.deltaNote: The set already exports the two statutory timing windows as named constants read by the lateness rule and by every hint that names a window (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-084, repo-plantsfrontend-p17-107).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants page reached from the overview ends with Save and continue and its own save-and-return control side by side as the only buttons in one button group, with its cancel link on its own line below the group; a page reached from another page ends with the primary button alone.
requirements.why: A trader sent from the overview can stop and go back to it from where they were sent, while a sub-page leaves the way the trader came in.
requirements.deltaNote: The shared save-actions partial already owns how every plants page ends, in that order (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-075, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-212).

requirements.statement: While a high-risk plants notification is being amended, every page except check your answers ends exactly as it does on a draft, and the status strip shows the Amend status with its Cancel amend link.
requirements.why: A trader amending a notification is doing the same work as a trader filling in a draft, so the page behaves the same way and only the strip says which it is.
requirements.deltaNote: A plants test already renders every task-row page in both states and fails if their endings differ (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-324).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants page answers a validation failure with HTTP 400, one error summary titled "There is a problem" carrying a link per field error, an "Error:" prefix on the page title, the message beside each field, and the trader's own answers kept.
requirements.why: A trader who gets something wrong sees what to fix without losing what they typed, and the status code tells a monitor the request was refused.
requirements.deltaNote: Plants already answers every validation failure with a 400 rather than the live animals mixture of 200s (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-072).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants page is built from GOV.UK Frontend and Ministry of Justice Frontend components and utility classes only, with no hand-rolled component and no custom CSS.
requirements.why: A tested government component is accessible and maintained, and a bespoke one has to be proved from scratch every time it changes.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants set already builds from the two toolboxes and refuses the live animals service's bespoke classes and totals panel (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-118).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants page is checked for accessibility on its first render and on its validation-error state against the five rule sets covering WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 A and AA, failing on any serious or critical violation, and no page narrows that list.
requirements.why: The machine-checkable 2.1 and 2.2 rules only run when their tags are asked for, and a page allowed to narrow the list would hide the very rules the service is held to.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants fit harness already builds its check with the five tags, so the ruling and the code agree (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-174).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants page is audited by Lighthouse from a registered route the seeding step can reach, under a report name no other route claims, on a seed shape whose own categories admit its country of origin, and the floors stay a performance score of 0.60 and accessibility and best-practices scores of 0.70 with no search-engine assertion.
requirements.why: A page whose prerequisites are unmet redirects and would silently audit the overview instead, and a lowered floor hides the regression it was put there to catch.
requirements.deltaNote: The audit scripts, the targets step and the three floors are already in the repository (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-172-m1 records them in place, and repo-plantsfrontend-p18-246 the floors).

requirements.statement: A change to the high-risk plants journey ends with the set test run, the whole-repo test run, the format check, the lint run and the feature browser suite green, and the whole-journey browser suite too when the change touches the whole journey or the shared browser helpers.
requirements.why: The set run does not cover composition, dispatch, the fulfilment registry or the copy checks, so a green set run alone can hide a broken journey.
requirements.deltaNote: The set's verification ladder already names those runs, and green already means every command exits zero with a suite that matched files (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-096, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-234).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants page carries browser coverage of its first render, a happy-path save and redirect, persistence on reload, every validation rule, the answers kept after an error, every error-summary link moving focus, Back, Save and return, Cancel and Change navigation, the purge when an answer leaves scope, its check-answers rows and its overview row states.
requirements.why: A change to a page's wording, layout or controls can break any of those without failing a unit test, so the page's own browser spec is where the change is proved.
requirements.deltaNote: The set's test conventions already require that list of a page's browser spec (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-094, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-325).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants page's Back link goes to the place the trader came from, carried on the link or the form rather than held in the session, falling back to the overview, to the dashboard on the first page until an answer is entered, and to the notification list on a submitted notification's review.
requirements.why: A trader who arrived from the overview, a Change link, a list card or the type question expects Back to return there, and a trail held in the session would get it wrong in a second tab.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants flow guide and ledger already hold this rule, with a trail of the newest forty places (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-113, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-105).

requirements.statement: A new high-risk plants page joins the journey's one page order and its task row, is filed in the caption map or listed there as bare, and is registered in the dispatch and routes barrels, its binding bundle and its review card.
requirements.why: Each of those registrations is checked at boot or by a test, so a page that misses one either fails to start the service or renders without its caption, its row or its review card.
requirements.deltaNote: The set's recipes already limit a new page's registration to those five steps, with a coverage test failing until the caption decision is made either way (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-338, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-304).

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants overview takes its groups from the journey's flow sections in order and appends the check-and-submit group, and a task row groups pages for submit readiness and decides nothing about where Save and continue goes.
requirements.why: Keeping the page order and the overview's grouping separate means a change to one does not silently move the other.
requirements.deltaNote: The set keeps feature group, flow section and task row as three separate things and derives the overview's groups from the sections (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-326, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-088).

requirements.statement: Save and return to overview on a high-risk plants page makes the same checks as Save and continue and changes only where a valid save goes.
requirements.why: Two buttons that save the same page must either both accept an answer or both refuse it, or a trader can save past a check by choosing the other button.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants records already describe it that way: the control posts a hub exit and runs the same validation with no opt-in (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-297).

requirements.statement: An answer on a high-risk plants notification that leaves scope is purged and never restored, scope is worked out afresh on every read and write rather than stored, and a page whose every question is out of scope is passed over by Save and continue.
requirements.why: A notification must hold only what its consignment needs, so an answer kept out of sight would be submitted as part of a record the trader was never shown.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants ledger already rules the wipe and the fresh evaluation on every read and write (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-062, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-103).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants place-of-destination or consignor picker lists its own role's addresses together with any address saved with no role, and the consignment contact picker asks for no role and lists every address in the book.
requirements.why: An address saved before the record carried roles would otherwise be invisible to the picker that needs it, and the contact can be any address the organisation holds.
requirements.deltaNote: Each plants picker already narrows the organisation's book to its own role plus any address saved with no role, and the stub book holds one such record to prove it (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-079, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-225).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants picker stores a copy of the record it picks, a later address-book edit or deletion never changes the notification, and a copied address that breaks the address rules makes check your answers refuse Continue and the declaration refuse Submit.
requirements.why: A submitted notification must say what the trader saw when they submitted it, while an address that can no longer be saved must not be carried into a submission unnoticed.
requirements.deltaNote: Plants already copies the chosen record onto the notification and refuses an id the book no longer holds, throwing on an address-book outage rather than reading it as a deletion (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-011, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-016, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-017).

requirements.statement: The organisation whose address book a high-risk plants picker reads comes only from the verified session, never from the submitted form.
requirements.why: Otherwise a trader could reach another organisation's addresses by posting an identifier.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants specification already records that the organisation is taken only from the verified session (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-079-m1).

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants journey keeps the behaviours its own specification records: its entry guard, its one page order, its save-and-return and Back rules, its scope purge, its two-page commodity collection, its own session cookies, its lenient page validation, its four system-populated values, its layout chrome and its boot guards.
requirements.why: They are the platform behaviour every plants page is built on, so a look-and-feel change is made inside them rather than against them.
requirements.deltaNote: The specification's behaviours block already holds all of them (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-060 to repo-plantsfrontend-p15-171).

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants journey keeps the data, validation and behaviour its own decisions ledger and conflicts register have settled: its commodity vocabulary and lists, the per-category origin narrowing, the per-line fields and their formats, the arrival matters, the identification numbers, the single contact pick, the declaration statements, the reference number, the four-value status vocabulary and the two timing windows.
requirements.why: Those decisions rest on the plants statute and policy paper rather than on any design, so a change made for look and feel leaves them exactly as they are.
requirements.deltaNote: The 97 ledger entries and the 40 register entries already hold these decisions, each subject carrying a pointer to the entry that settled it (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-001, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-009).

requirements.statement: A change to the high-risk plants frontend follows the set's own served-surface reference and its obligation-model, features, flow-and-gates, services, limits, copy-status, testing and Lighthouse guides, and its four recipes for adding a field, a page, a section and a collection.
requirements.why: The guides and recipes are how a plants change is made in that repository's conventions, and a change made some other way fails a boot guard, a convention test or a coverage test rather than merging quietly.
requirements.deltaNote: The set already carries the reference, the eight guides and the four recipes, with boot guards and coverage tests behind them (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-039-m1, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-287).

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants set's own engineering-hygiene increments stay the plants team's work: its continuous-integration parity and workflow fixes, the multi-architecture and non-gating-audit publish changes, the Lighthouse scripts, the dependency-update configuration, the architecture-lint baseline, the removal of the unused platform services, the collection exemplars, the documentation-drift sweep, the unauthorised view's copy and the dashboard's empty submitted date.
requirements.why: The goal is what a user sees in the journeys that exist, and the set's own build hygiene lies outside it; ten of these have in any case been done since the ledger recorded them.

requirements.statement: The drift between the high-risk plants set's records and its code stays as it stands wherever this programme changes neither: entries recording work already done, the entry-guard entry describing a condition the code does not have, the recipes and guides calling registration modules empty when they hold five sections and seven task rows, and the guides that disagree with each other about the flow-only keys and the captioned sections.
requirements.why: This programme keeps true the records of what it changes and no more; the owner has already declined one such tidy-up, and the rest is the plants team's own hygiene.

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants records' structural gaps stay as they are: the conflicts register has no state for an unsettled disagreement, no entry says who may reopen a ruling or on what evidence, the parked questions have no owner and no date, the panel evidence names no judge or chair and does not say which ledger entry each of its rulings became, and three of the five standing rulings are nowhere stated in their own words.
requirements.why: This programme keeps its own open questions and decisions in its own records, and the plants panel's evidence belongs to the work that produced it.

requirements.statement: The questions the high-risk plants set has parked stay parked: users, sign-in models, agents, delegation and plant-operator registration; internal-user login; bulk upload, importing from existing documents and reusing a previous consignment; regulator, inspector and analyst screens; list maintenance, risk classification and spot-check scheduling; document uploads; the outbox and event publishing; a combined animals and plants list; competent-authority routing; the notification reference's type-code prefix; the service name, feedback address and helpdesk lines; guidance and a before-you-start page; the previous scheme and the Northern Irish and Irish precedents; the lawful basis, privacy notice and retention period; a live Welsh service; a meaning for "sustainable"; and parity of internal access.
requirements.why: Each waits on a policy answer nobody has or on capability nobody is building, and the goal is the look and feel of the journeys that exist.

requirements.statement: Claims in this area's working set that state one plants page's own content, questions, options, hints or error messages are weighed in that page's area: the commodity type and commodity pages, origin, arrival status and arrival details, place of destination, the consignor and contact pickers, the identification numbers, the overview, check your answers, the declaration, the confirmation, the notification list, and the delete and cancel-amendment pages.
requirements.why: Each page's area reads the same claims against the plants code and the design, and one requirement per difference a user can see belongs there rather than in the record of what the set has settled.

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants journey keeps the four decisions its ledger has already landed in the code: no use, contact-number or contact-email obligation and no contact-details page, so the contact section is the one address-book pick; the commodity-type save keeps the lines the new type allows, counts the rest as removed and opens the commodities list with that count; the declaration carries its three plants statements, the last covering failing to notify, notifying late and giving incorrect details; and the arrival-status page asks whether the consignment has arrived in Great Britain.
requirements.why: A change made for the look of a page must not quietly undo a decision the set has already built, and these four are the ones where the ledger and the code have been checked against each other.
requirements.deltaNote: Each was checked against the code and found in place: the obligations manifest holds no use, contact-number or contact-email obligation and there is no contact-details feature folder; the commodity-type controller reconciles and redirects with the removed count; the declaration copy holds the three statements; and the arrival-status copy asks about Great Britain (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-178, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-179, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-180, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-181).

conflicts.about: Whether the one-form-each notification view header rule gives the high-risk plants frontend a Copy as new action, which the plants set has parked.

positions.says: The one-form-each header rule covers Amend, Copy as new and Delete on the notification view header, and applies in both the live animals frontend and the plants frontend.
Copy as new is left out of the plants view header because plants has parked it.
Plants offers View, Amend and Delete and no Copy as new anywhere, and reusing a previous consignment is parked with no increment of its own.

conflicts.outcome: Left open. The 19 November ruling names three header actions in both frontends, but plants has only two, so the rule cannot be met in plants as written; reading it as introducing the action would build a capability the plants set parks under its own standing ruling, and reading it as covering only what plants has leaves the later ruling partly unapplied. Nothing ranks the two readings.
conflicts.question: Does the one-form-each notification view header rule add a Copy as new action to the high-risk plants frontend, or apply only to the actions plants already has?
conflicts.default: The park stands and each part gets what it has: in the live animals frontend Amend and Copy as new each post their own form and Delete is a link to the delete confirmation page outside both; in the plants frontend Amend posts its own form, Delete is the same link outside it, and no Copy as new is built.

conflicts.about: Whether the high-risk plants journey spec ruling that was deleted rather than superseded is restored, as the set's own convention requires.

positions.says: A ruling changes only through a new numbered entry that supersedes the earlier one, which stays in the ledger marked superseded, and a ruling lives nowhere else.
The plants journey spec ruling that was deleted rather than superseded stays as it is, and the ruling records no interest in changing it.

conflicts.outcome: The 19 November ruling wins: the deleted plants journey spec ruling is not restored and nothing is added to record its removal. The set's convention is not set aside, because it still governs every entry this programme adds to the ledger, so no claim is overruled.

conflicts.about: Whether the high-risk plants address pickers keep the pagination and the restatement of the chosen address that their own records describe.

positions.says: Pagination is kept everywhere, every picker pages at eight and the restatement of the chosen address comes back, the plants contact picker included.
The plants address pickers lose their pagination and their 'Selected address' inset.
A plants picker shows eight addresses a page with pagination beyond that and an inset naming the address already chosen.

conflicts.outcome: The 25 November ruling wins over the 9 October afternoon claim, which it names as an error: every plants picker pages at eight and keeps the restatement of the chosen address. That is what the plants records already describe, so the plants records stand and the pickers need no ledger entry.

conflicts.about: Which high-risk plants pages are signed off, when the engine reads a maturity level from each page but the set's records do not say which page holds which level.

positions.says: A page's maturity is one of exploring, detailing, agreed or readyForLive, a page that sets none is treated as exploring, and a page at agreed or readyForLive counts as signed off.
The set's docs do not say which pages are at which maturity level, so they do not show which pages of the journey are signed off.

conflicts.outcome: Left open. An increment that changes a plants page has to know whether it is changing agreed behaviour, and the set's own records answer that for no page; the one source says both that the level decides it and that the level is not written down anywhere a reader can find it.
conflicts.question: Which high-risk plants pages are at agreed or readyForLive, so an increment that changes one knows it is changing a signed-off page?
conflicts.default: Each page's level is read from its own page identity module and nowhere else, and a page whose module names no level is treated as below agreed, so no plants change is held as a change to a signed-off page unless that page's own module says agreed or readyForLive.
